summary: Obfuscated npm loader fetches and executes remote code; ships iOS/macOS Mach-O implant binaries
details: @cdnshell/loader@0.0.20 declares itself as a 'static assets distribution' package but ships an obfuscated JavaScript bootstrap (a12i5u6l.js) alongside a tree of iOS/macOS Mach-O ARM64/ARM64e binaries under 03_payloads/ (agent_a64*, stager_a64_*, kbridge_a64*) and C2 dylibs under 04_c2/. The loader is heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style string-array indirection, custom base64+URI decoder, hex-mangled identifiers, control-flow shuffle, Symbol.for-hidden global export). It fetches manifest and engine modules over a runtime-configured base URL and executes fetched source via `new Function(source)()` (also `new Function(atob(b64))()` for base64-injected payloads), auto-invoked on document load and on a setInterval, with runtime-selected engine modules chosen from a host-capability probe table. Shipped Mach-O artifacts reference iOS private entitlements (com.apple.private.security.storage.DiagnosticReports.read), CoreTelephony/Photos/SQLite frameworks, and an install-name /usr/local/lib/SamplePayload.dylib, with version-per-directory (30/40/70/75/80/83/90) matching iOS major versions. package.json ships no dependencies, no scripts, no main, no bin, and no repository, while the tarball contains only obfuscated JS plus native implant binaries. The declared purpose does not describe or justify these contents; installing or loading the package exposes consumers to arbitrary remote-fetched code execution and stages platform-specific mobile-OS implants.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
